modelingNotes: 110 East, 110 East Blvd, South End, Charlotte — procedural, CC0-1.0. bun generators/clt-110-east.ts

A 23-storey speculative office tower (Stiles / Shorenstein, Hastings Architecture; topped out August 2023, delivered April 2024) beside the East/West Blvd light-rail station. Three things identify it: a plain, deep-blue glass box with pale floor lines; the parking podium below it (floors 2–10) wrapped in a silver perforated-metal screen whose top edge slants down toward the rail line, leaving the concrete deck edges bare above it; and the recessed 11th-floor amenity level, a dark gap between podium and tower with a terrace notch at the South Blvd / East Blvd corner.

Evidence: - OSM: way/1152461493 (outline, 23 levels, height "88w", read as 88 m), way/1278215436 (tower part, 10–88 m), way/1278215437 (south podium part, 10–32 m), way/1430326680 (podium, 10–32 m), way/1430326681 (ground floor, 0–10 m), way/1430326682–1430326694 (ground-floor columns, 10 m). - Published: 305 ft / 93 m, 23 storeys; floors 2–10 parking, 11 amenity and terrace, 12–23 offices (Wikipedia "110 East", Q115519219). - Lidar, USGS 3DEP NC Phase 4 Mecklenburg 2016 (1 m): flown when the site was a surface lot, so used for the ground only: the lot dips ~1.3 m below the surrounding sidewalks; y = 0 is that low point and the streets are taken at 1.3 m. - Photos (Wikimedia Commons, City Dweller 2, CC BY-SA 4.0): https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:110_East_Late_April_2024.jpg (from South Blvd, east) https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:110_East_at_the_corner_of_South_Blvd_and_East_Blvd_Mid-December_2025.jpg (east corner, the terrace notch) https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:110_East_viewed_from_Steel_Yard_along_the_South_End_Rail_Trail_Late_April_2024.jpg (south-west end, the bare deck above the screen) https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:110_East_along_East_Blvd_April_2024.jpg (East Blvd face: screen, lobby, garage entrance) https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:110_East_along_the_East_West_Blvd_Station_Late_April_2024.jpg (rail-trail face) https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:110_East_wide_view_March_2023.jpg (under construction: podium and core)

Heights above the street: the ground floor to 9.5 m (OSM 10), the podium to 32 m (OSM), the amenity level to 37 m (estimated, one tall storey), the offices to 89.5 m (twelve ~4.4 m floors, estimated), the mechanical screen to 93 m (published height). OSM's 88 m is taken as the roof without it. Estimated from photos: the slant of the screen (32 m along South Blvd, falling to 20 m at the north corner and 17 m at the west), the screen's foot (6 m), the terrace notch (two bays, the amenity storey), the setback of the amenity glass (1.5 m), mullion spacing.
Doubts: the screen's slant is simplified to one straight run per face; no photo shows the rail-trail face's upper podium squarely.
Model frame: bearing 34 (model +y runs north-east along the rail line toward East Blvd; +x is south-east, toward South Blvd); metres above the base.

Original procedural model from https://github.com/alexwohlbruck/landmarks (catalog id "clt-110-east", model "clt-110-east"), generated by https://github.com/alexwohlbruck/landmarks/blob/a1974bbf738c6994edbe99a7a61818b9d69da9e0/generators/clt-110-east.ts. That repository is the editable source; source.blend.gz is the exported mesh imported into Blender for convenience.

Exported for Open Landmarks v1: placement bearing and scale baked in; moving parts frozen in their rest pose; footings and basements below the lowest ground (y = 0) cut away; material colours carried over exactly, as library finishes where they are not standard swatches.
Window panels clipped to the walls behind them; 1092 m² of glazing with no wall behind it (curtain walls, glazing past a wall's edge) uses the clt-110-east-glazing finish in the window colour.
To fit six materials, folded clt-110-east-east-roof into clt-110-east-east-screen (ΔE 4.2).
